originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq rallies to sharply higher close; chip surge offsets Iran worries
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a good day, with the Nasdaq finishing higher than expected. This was largely due to technology companies that make computer chips, such as Micron, doing well because of a big investment plan related to artificial intelligence. Despite concerns about tensions between the US and Iran, the market still went up. The fact that jobless claims remained stable also helped, showing that the labor market is still strong. This positive news has investors looking forward to seeing how companies perform in the upcoming earnings season.

originalTitle: Groww responds to Nithin Kamath tweet: Direct mutual funds remain free for DIY investors
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Groww, an investment platform, is telling its users that they can still buy direct mutual funds without paying any extra fees. This means that people who like to manage their own investments (called "do-it-yourself" or DIY investors) can continue to use Groww's services for free. Groww made this announcement after some recent conversations about mutual funds in the market. This is good news for DIY investors who use Groww, as they won't have to pay any commissions on their mutual fund purchases. This reassurance from Groww helps investors know what to expect from the platform.

originalTitle: Sebi cancels registration of 12 research analysts over unpaid renewal fees
simplifiedContent: The stock market regulator, Sebi, has cancelled the licenses of 12 research analysts because they didn't pay their renewal fees. This means they can no longer provide research and advice to investors. Sebi took this action after sending them notices and not getting any response. The cancellation of their licenses is important because it helps maintain the integrity of the market by ensuring that only compliant and responsible analysts can operate. This action shows that Sebi is taking steps to enforce its rules and regulations.

originalTitle: HDFC Bank Q1 results date: Private lender to announce June quarter earnings on 18 July
simplifiedContent: HDFC Bank, a private lender, will announce its earnings for the quarter that ended in June on July 18. This is when the company will share its financial results for the first quarter of the financial year 2027. The bank's Board of Directors will meet on July 18 to review and approve these results. This announcement is important because it will give investors an idea of how the bank performed in the last quarter. The results will be closely watched by investors, as they will provide insight into the bank's financial health.

originalTitle: Russia's largest private lender Alfa Bank tests crypto trading, plans suite of crypto services ahead of govt legislation
simplifiedContent: Alfa Bank, a big bank in Russia, is trying out a new feature that lets people buy and sell cryptocurrencies on its investment app. The bank is also planning to offer more services related to cryptocurrencies in the future. This is happening before the Russian government creates new rules and laws about digital assets. This matters because it shows that a major bank is interested in cryptocurrencies and wants to get involved before the government sets its rules. By doing this, Alfa Bank is preparing to offer its customers more options for investing in cryptocurrencies.

originalTitle: Multibagger defence stock Apollo Micro Systems to be in focus on Friday; here's why
simplifiedContent: Apollo Micro Systems, a company that makes products for the defense industry, is making a big move by buying a large part of another company called Premier Explosives. They're spending ₹1,550 crore to buy 41.33% of Premier Explosives' shares, which could help India's defense capabilities. This deal might also include buying more shares from other owners of Premier Explosives. The acquisition is expected to be completed by December 2026. This news might make Apollo Micro Systems' stock more interesting to investors on Friday.
